column1: # The file device's traces: what its runtime's end owes a core (abi/fs.json,
# ARCHITECTURE.md's files), apart from the boundary's rules 0 to 8 — the boundary
# carries the calls, and this is what they mean. Run against the runtime's end
# (ts/runtime/src/io/fs.test.ts): a step writes a record as a core's turn would, `turn`
# runs them as the runtime does after a turn, and what reaches the core is held to the trace.
# A path P is a JSON array of its tokens, each a number or a string: `[7,"a"]`. A token is an
# i32 or a string; a trace writes a float or an integer past an i32 to see it refused.
#   file P B          the binding's file P: its bytes in hex, ENOENT, or `later` — answered
#                     only when a `deliver` says, as a transport answers
#   refuse P ERRNO    the binding refuses to commit the file P, with ERRNO by name
#   open FD P FLAG    a core's FS_OPEN tagged FD, as the core issued it (slot and
#                     generation); FLAG O_RDONLY, O_WRONLY (io/fs.json `flag`) or a number
#   read FD N [AT]    a core's FS_READ tagged FD, of N bytes into the core's memory at AT,
#                     or at the trace's own place without it
#   write FD TEXT     a core's FS_WRITE of TEXT, tagged FD
#   turn              the runtime runs the turn's records
#   deliver P B       the transport answers what `later` held, with B as `file` takes it
#   expect opened FD RES   the next completion the core is sent, of an open: a size, or an errno by name
#   expect closed FD RES   the next, of a close: 0, or an errno by name
#   expect quiet      no completion the core has not been held to
#   expect read HEX   what the last read put in the core's memory
#   expect commit P TEXT   what a write made the file
#   expect unwritten P     that no write reached the file
# An open's completion comes on a later turn, however much later: `later` is how a trace says the
# transport is slow, and nothing here fixes how many turns pass. Each open and each close is
# completed once. Run against the device's runtime too (xpute-runtime native/serve.test.rs).

column2: open.later open.absent open.flag token.negative token.max token.float token.wide read read.fault read.zero read.unknown read.wronly write write.denied write.rdonly close.opening close.unknown stale.reuse
